author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Elaine Pelino filed for a recount Thursday in Rhode Island’s close Republican primary for governor, adding a formal review request to a contest that remained unresolved after election night.

NBC 10 reported that unofficial Board of Elections results showed Aaron Guckian leading Pelino by 279 votes. The posted totals gave Guckian 11,623 votes, or 50.61%, and Pelino 11,344 votes, or 49.4%, based on results updated early Thursday.

State rules required primary recount applications to be submitted by 4 p.m. on the day after the election. The Board of Elections reviews an application to determine whether the contest qualifies. Any recount would take place at the board’s Cranston office and would be open to the public.

Guckian, a trade-association executive, was the Republican nominee for lieutenant governor in 2022 and has the state party’s endorsement. Pelino is a first-time candidate. The eventual winner will advance to the November general election. The posted margin and totals remain unofficial while the recount request is considered.
dek: Unofficial results showed Aaron Guckian ahead by 279 votes as the Board of Elections prepared to review the application.
headline: Elaine Pelino requests recount in Rhode Island governor primary
